arcs.title: Arcs and guides
arcs.description: Smooth connected support curves with optional guides.

paired.title: Paired rails
paired.description: Plain support curves with their full opposing guides retained from near the start of each support. Both rails participate in the physics search; unused guide sections remain visible.

segments.title: Scattered · original
segments.description: The original velocity-feedback controller, retained as a comparison.

scattered.title: Scattered · improved
scattered.description: Tests measured contact fragments against the original scattered controller using the remaining allowance.

waves.title: Wave curves
waves.description: A returning bend followed by an independently shaped exit.

facets.title: Faceted curves
facets.description: Long straight faces, searched with their actual angular geometry.

serpentine.title: Serpentine rails
serpentine.description: One broad S-shaped sweep: the curve bends one way, then the other.

terraces.title: Terraced rails
terraces.description: Two eased steps interrupt the slope, making ledges and rounded transitions.

scallops.title: Ripple rails
scallops.description: Two successive waves along the support, creating a repeating undulation.

ribbon.title: Ribbed ribbons
ribbon.description: Curved bands divided by ribs. All outer edges and ribs are physical normal lines, present during search.

teeth.title: Crystal teeth
teeth.description: Triangular teeth grow away from the supporting rail and its guide. The complete structure participates in physics.

petals.title: Petal chains
petals.description: Rounded lobes grow along the supporting curves, creating a repeating floral outline. Every edge is physical.

plan.note: Eight functional geometry choices plus the original scattered controller for comparison. Paired rails retain the complete opposing guides that ordinary arcs trim after replay. Outlined contour experiments remain archived separately. Shapes are constructed before physics search. Matched short passages, not a benchmark headline. Improved scattered construction compares two normal-segment methods; its choice and all work are recorded. No arc track is substituted for scattered geometry. Wall times include lazy model loading; first cell is cold, later cells reuse the process.

interpretation: Research passages, not a canonical headline. Development inputs and evaluation inputs are identified in the accompanying study report. No broad generalization or visual approval claim. Wall times include shared-host contention and model loading.
